verdict.inspectionLimits: panel-96 supports geometry-level review. panel-24 supports silhouette/merge review only. panel-16 supports blob-level review only; per-row defect attribution at 16 is inferred from 96 geometry plus what survives in the 16 strip, not directly resolved.

rows.subject: clock, no modifier
rows.curveAndCounterQuality: Ring is a clean continuous circle at 96 with even stroke weight; hand junction meets at the pivot with no overshoot. Face counter is the largest in the set and stays open at 24.
rows.at24: Ring, counter and both hands survive; hands stay separable.
rows.at16: Silhouette and ring counter survive. Hands converge toward a single mark but the icon still reads as a clock.

rows.subject: clock + plus badge
visibleDefects: A short horizontal stroke sits in the lower half of the clock face, detached from the hand pivot, in BOTH the outlined and filled variants. It does not terminate on the ring or on the hand junction, so it reads as a stray/orphaned segment rather than a hand.

In the filled variant the plus badge abuts the disc with little to no keepout: the badge's inboard arm fuses into the black mass, so the plus loses its cross silhouette and reads as a lump on the disc edge.
The ring interruption around the badge is not cleanly registered to the badge in the outlined variant - the opening and the badge footprint do not line up, leaving an ambiguous stub of ring.
rows.modifierReadability: Poor. Recognisable as a plus at 96 outlined only; the filled variant already degrades at 96 and the badge is not separable at 24.
rows.curveAndCounterQuality: Ring curvature itself is fine. The failure is in the internal marks and the badge keepout, not the arc.
rows.at24: Gaps: badge keepout does not survive in filled. Counters: face counter survives outlined, closes around the stray stroke. Modifier arms: do not survive - plus becomes a bulge.
rows.at16: No. Badge merges fully into the disc; the stray stroke and hands collapse into one blot.

rows.subject: card/window + lock badge
visibleDefects: The parent contour is interrupted at the lower-LEFT, on the opposite side of the artwork from the lock badge at lower-right. Nothing occupies that opening, so it is not badge clearance - it is an unexplained open contour.
In the filled variant that same opening renders as a white wedge/slot biting into the solid body, which reads as a chip or rendering artifact rather than a designed negative shape.
rows.modifierReadability: Lock is readable at 96 in both variants; the shackle arch counter is small and is the first thing to close at 24.
rows.curveAndCounterQuality: Corner radii on the parent rect are consistent and the top band is square to the body. The wedge's curved edge does not match the parent corner radius, which is why it reads as foreign.
rows.at24: Gaps: the badge keepout survives; the lower-left opening survives but as an ambiguous notch. Counters: shackle counter closes or nearly closes. Modifier arms: lock body survives as a shape, shackle does not reliably.
rows.at16: No. Body reads as a rounded slab; badge and notch both reduce to edge irregularities.

rows.subject: window with dot row + lock badge
visibleDefects: Same unexplained lower-left contour opening as row C, and it is more pronounced here: in the filled variant it is a large curved white wedge intruding into the body, the most conspicuous single artifact in the panel.
The three-dot row is the finest detail in the set and its inter-dot gaps do not hold at 24.
The wedge's arc is tangent to nothing in the parent geometry - it neither follows the corner radius nor clears the badge.
rows.modifierReadability: Lock readable at 96, marginal at 24. The dot row is a secondary detail, not a modifier, and it is the first element lost.
rows.curveAndCounterQuality: Parent rect is clean; the intruding wedge is the defect. Dot counters are undersized relative to the rest of the family.
rows.at24: Gaps: dot separations do not survive. Counters: dots merge toward a dash. Modifier arms: lock survives as a mass, shackle does not.
rows.at16: No. Reduces to a slab with a bite out of it.

rows.subject: clock + plus badge
visibleDefects: Minor: at 24 the plus arms thin toward the rendering floor; the badge reads as a plus but with reduced arm contrast. Not a geometry defect.
rows.modifierReadability: Good. Plus is separable from the parent in both variants at 96 and at 24.
rows.curveAndCounterQuality: Ring arc is clean and the interruption is a single clean-terminated arc registered to the badge - valid clearance, not a collision. Filled variant carries a genuine white keepout between disc and badge. Hands meet at the pivot with no stray segment.
rows.at24: Gaps: keepout survives in both variants. Counters: face counter survives. Modifier arms: survive.
rows.at16: Borderline. Badge survives as a detectable protrusion; the plus crossbars are no longer separable and the hands merge.

rows.subject: card with stripe + lock badge
visibleDefects: Minor: the shackle counter of the lock is small and closes at 24, leaving the badge reading as a padlock silhouette rather than a resolved padlock. Consistent with rows C and D, so it is a family-wide floor, not an F-specific fault.
rows.modifierReadability: Good. The badge sits at the outer bottom-right corner with clearance adjacent to it, so it is separable from the parent at 24 in both variants.
rows.curveAndCounterQuality: Parent contour is closed except for the badge-adjacent interruption, which is clean-terminated and correctly registered - intentional clearance. Corner radii consistent; stripe is parallel to the body edge with even offsets. No stray or unexplained negative shapes in either variant.
rows.at24: Gaps: badge clearance survives. Counters: stripe counter survives; shackle counter closes. Modifier arms: lock body survives.
rows.at16: Borderline. Card silhouette and badge bump survive; the stripe flattens toward the body.

comparisons.B_vs_E: E is the stronger execution of the same concept. Both interrupt the ring for a plus badge; E's interruption is clean-terminated and registered to the badge, and E's filled variant preserves a keepout so the plus stays a distinct cross. B's filled variant fuses the plus into the disc, and B carries an orphaned horizontal stroke inside the face that E does not. This is a defect difference, not a stylistic one.
comparisons.C_vs_F: F is the stronger execution. Both are a rounded card with a lower-right lock badge. F's only contour interruption is adjacent to the badge and is therefore valid clearance; C's interruption is on the opposite side from its badge, clears nothing, and in the filled variant becomes a wedge-shaped intrusion whose curvature does not match the parent radius. C's badge is also inset rather than corner-anchored, which costs it separation at 24. Both share the same shackle-counter floor, so that is not a differentiator.

familyNotes: Rows C and D share the identical lower-left open-contour defect, which supports it being a systematic construction issue rather than a one-off.
The padlock shackle counter closes at 24 in every row that uses it (C, D, F). That is a badge-scale issue affecting the whole family.
All three panels are the same artwork at three sizes; no row shows evidence of size-specific geometry and none is claimed.

spatialFalseClaims: C and D describe lower-left interruption even though badge clearance is at right
B describes an orphan horizontal hand in both paints; outlined path has joined hand geometry
